ballot.album: Art Blakey & The Jazz Messengers — Free for All (1964)
ballot.case_for: Recorded in 1964, this is unequivocally in-scope hard bop: a single-session Van Gelder date led by Blakey with Wayne Shorter, Freddie Hubbard, Curtis Fuller, Cedar Walton, and Reggie Workman (S1). Its claim is not merely the famous title performance but a definitive document of the 1961–64 Messengers sextet at maximum force, joining exceptional personnel gravity to Shorter and Hubbard compositions and an immediately legible, thrilling discovery experience. The dossier records recognition through Penguin Guide, DownBeat, and AllMusic ratings, while Blue Note calls it Blakey's "arguably ... most dynamic album" and a "transcendent four-track album" (S2); taken together, these support its standing as a hard-bop summit.
ballot.case_against: The principal reservation is representational rather than musical: Moanin' is the broader public-facing defining statement of the Jazz Messengers and the record most directly associated with fixing their hard-bop identity. Free for All can therefore be heard as the extraordinary culmination of an established approach, rather than a necessary second Blakey entry if the canon is tightly limited and already covers Blakey, Shorter, and Hubbard elsewhere. Its consensus documentation is also thinner than ideal: the dossier relays ratings through Wikipedia and relies on a label spotlight, without direct Penguin, DownBeat, or independent-review text.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes that John treat Free for All as a consensus-core, strong-priority addition for representing the peak intensity and personnel of the early-1960s Jazz Messengers.
